1	#ifndef SG_FUSED_SM90_PARALLEL_CONFIG_CUH_
2	#define SG_FUSED_SM90_PARALLEL_CONFIG_CUH_
3	// ============================================================================
4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/parallel_config.cuh — the COMPILE-TIME parallelism point
5	// (the metaprogrammed template the L3-TC megakernel is specialized over).
6	//
7	// IMPLEMENTS: /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §1.1 (the ParConfig<DP,TP,PP,
8	// SP,ZeROStage> struct + the SingleGPU alias) and §1.2 (the bit-identical
9	// single-GPU contract — the kEmitComm gate that makes every comm branch fold
10	// away to ZERO code when the config is degenerate).
11	//
12	// HEADER-ONLY, SELF-CONTAINED, device+host. Included by every megakernel TU
13	// (decoder/vit/mamba) so the SAME translation unit can hold BOTH the single-GPU
14	// point AND a multi-GPU flagship point in one fat binary (design §1.2 — the
15	// discriminator is a TEMPLATE PARAMETER, not a TU-wide macro, because the
16	// campaign ships the single-GPU artifact alongside the 4D+ZeRO-3 flagship).
17	//
18	// WHY constexpr-everything: ALL fields are `static constexpr`, so every branch
19	// that reads them (`if constexpr (Par::kEmitComm)`, `if constexpr (Par::
20	// kShardOptGrad)`, …) folds at compile time. For the degenerate SingleGPU point
21	// the compiler emits NO NVSHMEM symbols, NO extra barriers, NO `comm` reads ⇒
22	// `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt, SingleGPU>` is byte-for-byte identical to
23	// today's `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt>` (design §1.2, the PTX-diff gate).
24	//
25	// THIS FILE ADDS NO MATH AND NO COMM. It is the pure compile-time config carrier
26	// + an empty CommCtx POD (the megakernel's default `comm` argument; populated
27	// with NCCL/NVSHMEM handles ONLY on the kEmitComm path, which a kernel builder
28	// wires later — out of scope here). Authored 1-GPU/CPU per design §7.
29	// ============================================================================
30	
31	#include <cstdint>
32	
33	namespace sg { namespace fused { namespace par {
34	
35	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
36	//  ZeRO stage (design §1.1). Z0=none, Z1=opt-state shard, Z2=+grad shard,
37	//  Z3=+param shard. The flagship ships Z3 (design DELIVERABLE line); Z2 is the
38	//  SAME code path with param-sharding off (a stage flag), the first bring-up
39	//  increment (design §3.1).
40	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
41	enum class ZeROStage : int { Z0 = 0, Z1 = 1, Z2 = 2, Z3 = 3 };
42	
43	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	//  ParConfig — the compile-time ADAPTIVE 3D–5D(+ZeRO) parallelism point.
45	//
46	//  The (DP, TP, PP, SP, EP) tuple + ZeRO maps 1:1 to the Python-side
47	//  ParallelConfig (distributed.py: data/tensor/pipeline/expert_parallel +
48	//  zero_stage) per design §1.3. ALL fields constexpr ⇒ every consumer branch
49	//  folds; the degenerate point emits zero comm code (design §1.2).
50	//
51	//  ADAPTIVE DEGREE (the auto-3D–5D contract): the FRONT-END picks the degree and
52	//  instantiates the matching point (grokking_optimizers.parallel.auto_config,
53	//  /workspace/impl_diffs/adaptive_parallelism.md §3):
54	//    * base 3D  = DP × TP × PP                (every model);
55	//    * +SP (4th) iff the model is a SEQUENCE model (decoder / ViT-patches /
56	//      Mamba) — EXPRESSIBLE but pinned 1 this campaign (seq 4-17 makes a split
57	//      moot; the static_assert below is the loud gate);
58	//    * +EP (5th) iff the model declares EXPERTS (a model-level MoE, num_experts>1).
59	//      EP is the 6th TEMPLATE PARAM and is DEFAULTED to 1 so EVERY existing
60	//      5-arg ParConfig<DP,TP,PP,SP,Z> instantiation (the SingleGPU alias, the
61	//      §7.2 allow-list, the megakernel's Par=SingleGPU default) is BYTE-IDENTICAL
62	//      — EP=1 ⇒ kEPComm==false ⇒ every expert-dispatch branch folds to ZERO code
63	//      (the design §1.2 PTX-diff gate, extended to EP). EP is positioned AFTER Z
64	//      precisely so the trailing default preserves every current call site.
65	//
66	//  SP (sequence-parallel) is EXPRESSIBLE but pinned to 1 this campaign: at the
67	//  race's seq 4-17 a sequence split is moot (design §1.1 / PARALLELISM-FINAL),
68	//  so the static_assert below makes any SP!=1 instantiation a loud BUILD error
69	//  rather than a silently-broken path. EP is gated the SAME way TP is (a runtime-
70	//  degree axis, no fixed-to-1 assert) so a future MoE model instantiates EP>1
71	//  cleanly; the current dense roster never does (it has no model experts), so EP
72	//  stays 1 and folds away — honest inertness, not a stub that pretends to run.
73	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
74	template <int DP, int TP, int PP, int SP, ZeROStage Z, int EP = 1>
75	struct ParConfig {
76	    static constexpr int        kDP   = DP;   // data-parallel replicas
77	    static constexpr int        kTP   = TP;   // tensor-parallel ranks (Megatron col/row split)
78	    static constexpr int        kPP   = PP;   // pipeline stages
79	    static constexpr int        kSP   = SP;   // sequence-parallel (kept EXPRESSIBLE, fixed 1)
80	    static constexpr int        kEP   = EP;   // expert-parallel ranks (MoE; DEFAULT 1 = dense)
81	    static constexpr ZeROStage  kZeRO = Z;
82	
83	    // ── Derived compile-time gates (design §1.1). These are the predicates the
84	    //    megakernel + sharded-opt kernel branch on with `if constexpr`. ────────
85	    //    EP folds into kIsSingleGPU/kEmitComm so an EP>1 point is (correctly) a
86	    //    multi-GPU point (kEmitComm==true) and a dense EP==1 point with all other
87	    //    axes 1 is still the byte-identical SingleGPU (kIsSingleGPU==true).
88	    static constexpr bool kIsSingleGPU = (DP == 1 && TP == 1 && PP == 1 && SP == 1 && EP == 1);
89	    static constexpr bool kEmitComm     = !kIsSingleGPU;        // gate ALL NVSHMEM/NCCL
90	    static constexpr bool kShardParams  = (Z == ZeROStage::Z3);  // ZeRO-3 param residency shard
91	    static constexpr bool kShardOptGrad = (Z >= ZeROStage::Z2);  // ZeRO>=2 grad+opt-state shard
92	                                                                 // ⇒ kernel early-exits at B2 (§2.2)
93	    static constexpr bool kTPComm       = (TP > 1);             // in-kernel TP all-reduce (§5)
94	    static constexpr bool kPPStage      = (PP > 1);             // pipeline stage cut (§4)
95	    static constexpr bool kEPComm       = (EP > 1);             // in-kernel expert all-to-all (§2.4)
96	                                                                 // — folds to ZERO when EP==1 (dense)
97	
98	    // SP is expressible but must be 1 this campaign (design §1.1 static_assert).
99	    static_assert(SP == 1, "SP axis is expressible but must be 1 this campaign "
100	                           "(seq 4-17 makes a seq split moot; #14 / PARALLELISM-FINAL).");
101	    static_assert(DP >= 1 && TP >= 1 && PP >= 1 && SP >= 1 && EP >= 1, "degrees must be >= 1");
102	};
103	
104	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
105	//  THE single-GPU guarantee, named once so the static_asserts read cleanly
106	//  (design §1.1). `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt, SingleGPU>` MUST be
107	//  byte-identical to the legacy `<Opt>` overload — enforced by kEmitComm==false
108	//  folding every comm branch away (design §1.2). This is the default template
109	//  arg of the megakernel, so existing call sites compile unchanged.
110	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
111	using SingleGPU = ParConfig<1, 1, 1, 1, ZeROStage::Z0>;
112	
113	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
114	//  SizeConfig — the COMPILE-TIME *workload-size* point, the SECOND specialization
115	//  axis the megakernel is templated over (alongside ParConfig). It is the SAME
116	//  if-constexpr-on-config mechanism that gates the distributed all-reduce
117	//  (if constexpr (Par::kTPComm)), now keyed on workload SIZE rather than
118	//  parallelism: a LARGE config folds in CTA-TILING (occupancy>1 / clusters — more
119	//  CTAs per output tile to fill the SMs and kill the ~20% grid-barrier idle that
120	//  cross-CTA load imbalance causes at d=2048, bottleneck LEVER 2); a SMALL config
121	//  folds in NONE of it (the persistent 1-CTA/SM shape wins — overhead dominates).
122	//
123	//  ALL fields `static constexpr` ⇒ every consumer branch (`if constexpr
124	//  (Sz::kCtaTile)`, `if constexpr (Sz::kClusterDim > 1)`, …) folds at compile time.
125	//  The degenerate `SizeSmall` point sets every predicate to the SHIPPED value, so
126	//  `fused_decoder_megakernel_tc<Opt, Par, SizeSmall>` is byte-for-byte the pre-Sz
127	//  kernel — the PTX-diff gate (test_decoder_tc.py). This mirrors ParConfig's §1.2
128	//  byte-identical-when-degenerate contract exactly.
129	//
130	//  The selector that PICKS a SizeConfig from (d, layers, T, n_sms) lives host-side
131	//  in grokking_optimizers/megakernel_codegen.py::decoder_knobs_for_size (it also
132	//  emits the matching -DSG_TUNED_* tile knobs), keeping ONE source of truth for the
133	//  size→knobs map the same way ParallelConfig (distributed.py) is the source for
134	//  the parallelism degrees. This header carries ONLY the compile-time point + the
135	//  predicates the kernel branches on; it adds NO math and NO launch policy.
136	//
137	//  CtaTile           : the master gate — emit the CTA-tiled (occupancy>1) body
138	//                      (false on SizeSmall ⇒ the 1-CTA/SM persistent shape).
139	//  CtasPerTile       : how many CTAs cooperate on ONE output tile when CtaTile
140	//                      (1 on SizeSmall; e.g. 2 on SizeLarge). Drives the split of
141	//                      the per-tile GEMM N-range across cooperating CTAs (§7).
142	//  ClusterDim        : the Hopper thread-block-cluster size (1 = no cluster). A
143	//                      cluster lets cooperating CTAs share a distributed-smem tile
144	//                      + a cluster barrier instead of the grid barrier (§7); 1 on
145	//                      SizeSmall keeps the non-cluster launch byte-identical.
146	//  TileN             : the wgmma N-tile the body sizes from. Defaults to the
147	//                      SG_TUNED_TILE_N macro so SizeSmall == the shipped tile; a
148	//                      large tier may pin a different TileN as a constexpr (the
149	//                      kernel reads Sz::kTileN where it reads SG_TUNED_TILE_N
150	//                      today — see EDIT C note; on SizeSmall they are EQUAL so the
151	//                      substitution is byte-identical).
152	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
153	template <bool CtaTile, int CtasPerTile, int ClusterDim, int TileN>
154	struct SizeConfig {
155	    static constexpr bool kCtaTile     = CtaTile;     // master gate: occupancy>1 body
156	    static constexpr int  kCtasPerTile = CtasPerTile; // CTAs cooperating per output tile
157	    static constexpr int  kClusterDim  = ClusterDim;  // Hopper cluster size (1 = none)
158	    static constexpr int  kTileN       = TileN;       // wgmma N-tile the body sizes from
159	
160	    // Derived gate: a cluster launch is only meaningful when CTA-tiling is on AND
161	    // the cluster dim > 1. SizeSmall ⇒ false ⇒ no cluster launch attribute emitted.
162	    static constexpr bool kUseCluster = (CtaTile && ClusterDim > 1);
163	
164	    static_assert(CtasPerTile >= 1, "CtasPerTile must be >= 1");
165	    static_assert(ClusterDim  >= 1, "ClusterDim must be >= 1 (1 = no cluster)");
166	    static_assert(TileN       >= 1, "TileN must be >= 1");
167	    // CtaTile==false MUST be the degenerate (byte-identical) point: no cooperation,
168	    // no cluster. Guard it so a SizeSmall-shaped config can never silently request
169	    // tiling without flipping the master gate (the §1.2-style invariant).
170	    static_assert(CtaTile || (CtasPerTile == 1 && ClusterDim == 1),
171	                  "SizeConfig: CtaTile==false is the degenerate 1-CTA/SM point and "
172	                  "MUST have CtasPerTile==1 && ClusterDim==1 (byte-identical default).");
173	};
174	
175	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
176	//  SizeSmall — the DEGENERATE size point (the analogue of SingleGPU). CtaTile OFF,
177	//  1 CTA/tile, no cluster, TileN == the shipped SG_TUNED_TILE_N. This is the
178	//  DEFAULT template arg of the megakernel ⇒ every existing call site compiles
179	//  unchanged AND `<Opt, Par, SizeSmall>` is byte-for-byte the legacy kernel.
180	//
181	//  SizeSmall reads SG_TUNED_TILE_N so the size point inherits whatever tile the
182	//  autotuner pinned for the small tier; if SG_TUNED_TILE_N is unset it is the
183	//  in-header #ifndef default (128), matching model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh.
184	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
185	#ifndef SG_TUNED_TILE_N
186	#define SG_TUNED_TILE_N 128   // keep in sync with model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh #ifndef
187	#endif
188	using SizeSmall = SizeConfig</*CtaTile=*/false, /*CtasPerTile=*/1,
189	                             /*ClusterDim=*/1,   /*TileN=*/SG_TUNED_TILE_N>;
190	
191	// SizeLarge — the LARGE tier point: CTA-tiling ON, 2 CTAs per output tile, a 2-CTA
192	// Hopper cluster, the shipped TileN. This is the point the launcher selects for the
193	// d=2048 bench / flagship-class workloads (the codegen selector decides WHEN; see
194	// megakernel_codegen.decoder_knobs_for_size). It only ever instantiates the §7
195	// CTA-tiled body — NOT compiled until §7 lands, but the alias is defined now so the
196	// dispatch allow-list + the autotuner can name it. (Until §7, the kernel's
197	// `if constexpr (Sz::kCtaTile)` arm is the NO-OP stub of EDIT C.3 — instantiating
198	// SizeLarge compiles to the same body as SizeSmall, just reachable for wiring.)
199	using SizeLarge = SizeConfig</*CtaTile=*/true, /*CtasPerTile=*/2,
200	                             /*ClusterDim=*/2,  /*TileN=*/SG_TUNED_TILE_N>;
201	
202	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
203	//  CommCtx — the megakernel's default trailing argument (design §1.1 kernel
204	//  signature: `par::CommCtx comm /* default-constructed, unused when
205	//  !kEmitComm */`). It is an EMPTY POD here on purpose:
206	//
207	//   * On the SingleGPU / kEmitComm==false path the kernel never reads it, so the
208	//     ABI of the `<Opt>`-only overload is preserved (the old non-Par launcher
209	//     forwards a default-constructed CommCtx) and the PTX is unchanged.
210	//   * On the kEmitComm==true path a kernel builder widens this POD with the
211	//     NVSHMEM team handle / NCCL comm / tp_group rank table / peer param-shard
212	//     base pointers the in-kernel collectives need (design §5.2/§6.1). That
213	//     widening is GPU-window work and is intentionally NOT authored here (this
214	//     file is 1-GPU/CPU pre-work per design §7); the empty struct is the stable
215	//     seam those fields hang off without touching any single-GPU call site.
216	//
217	//  Trivially constructible/copyable so it is a valid by-value kernel parameter
218	//  and a no-cost default argument.
219	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
220	struct CommCtx {
221	    // rank within the world / the per-axis groups (filled only when kEmitComm).
222	    // Defaults describe the degenerate single-GPU world so a default-constructed
223	    // CommCtx is the correct "no comm" value the single-GPU path forwards.
224	    int world_size = 1;
225	    int world_rank = 0;
226	    int dp_size = 1, dp_rank = 0;
227	    int tp_size = 1, tp_rank = 0;
228	    int pp_size = 1, pp_rank = 0;
229	    // Opaque handle slots (NVSHMEM team / NCCL comm) — left as nullptr-able
230	    // pointers a builder casts to the concrete handle type behind kEmitComm, so
231	    // this header need NOT include <nccl.h>/<nvshmem.h> (kept CPU-compilable).
232	    // tp_comm_handle carries the NVSHMEM TP team id stored as
233	    // reinterpret_cast<void*>((intptr_t)nvshmem_team_t) (tp_team_t is int32_t);
234	    // tp::make_transport_from_comm reverses the cast (tp_kernel.md §3 A.2).
235	    void* tp_comm_handle = nullptr;   // NCCL comm / NVSHMEM TP team id (§5)
236	    void* dp_comm_handle = nullptr;   // NCCL comm for the DP group (reduce-scatter / all-gather)
237	    // ── In-kernel TP all-reduce wiring (filled ONLY on kEmitComm; nullptr/0 on
238	    //    the SingleGPU path, so a default-constructed CommCtx forwards "no TP
239	    //    heap" and the kEmitComm=false megakernel never reads these — the ABI of
240	    //    the default <Opt,SingleGPU> instantiation is preserved, the §6 PTX gate).
241	    //  * tp_sym_heap: the nvshmem_malloc'd SYMMETRIC base for the TP reduce slots
242	    //    (NOT the cudaMalloc workspace — /workspace/impl_diffs/tp_kernel.md §2/EDIT E).
243	    //    Opaque float* here; NvshmemTransport reinterprets it as heap_base. On the
244	    //    loopback build it is the strided cudaMalloc heap (LoopbackTransport).
245	    //  * tp_heap_stride_floats: per-PE symmetric stride (== tp::tp_heap_stride_floats).
246	    //  * tp_team_local_pe / tp_team_n_pes: the team-local pe index + team size
247	    //    (== nvshmem_team_my_pe / _n_pes on the TP team; == tp_rank / tp_size).
248	    void*   tp_sym_heap           = nullptr;  // nvshmem_malloc'd symmetric TP-slot base
249	    int64_t tp_heap_stride_floats = 0;        // per-PE symmetric stride (floats)
250	    int     tp_team_local_pe      = 0;        // pe-in-TP-team (== tp_rank)
251	    int     tp_team_n_pes         = 1;        // TP team size  (== tp_size)
252	    // ── In-kernel EXPERT-PARALLEL (MoE) wiring — the EP analogue of the TP block,
253	    //    filled ONLY when kEPComm (EP>1); nullptr/0 on every dense path. Mirrors
254	    //    the TP fields EXACTLY so a future expert all-to-all/dispatch reads its
255	    //    own symmetric heap + team the SAME way the TP reduce reads the TP team
256	    //    (/workspace/impl_diffs/adaptive_parallelism.md §2.4). A default-constructed
257	    //    CommCtx forwards "no EP" and the kEPComm=false megakernel never reads
258	    //    these — so the dense (EP==1) ABI is byte-identical (the EP PTX gate).
259	    //  * ep_comm_handle: the NVSHMEM EP team id stored as
260	    //    reinterpret_cast<void*>((intptr_t)nvshmem_team_t) (int32 team), reversed
261	    //    by a future ep::make_transport_from_comm — the SAME opaque-void* trick
262	    //    tp_comm_handle uses so this header needs no <nvshmemx.h>.
263	    //  * ep_sym_heap / ep_heap_stride_floats: the symmetric base + per-PE stride
264	    //    for the expert dispatch/combine token buffers (the all-to-all operands).
265	    //  * ep_team_local_pe / ep_team_n_pes: the EP-team-local pe + team size
266	    //    (== nvshmem_team_my_pe / _n_pes on the EP team; == ep_rank / ep_size).
267	    //    The EP team is the set of DP peers that together hold one full expert set
268	    //    (distributed.py _build_mesh ep_ranks — EP sub-divides DP, never enlarges
269	    //    world_size), so on the dense roster ep_team_n_pes==1 and this is inert.
270	    void*   ep_comm_handle        = nullptr;  // NCCL comm / NVSHMEM EP team id (§2.4)
271	    void*   ep_sym_heap           = nullptr;  // nvshmem_malloc'd symmetric EP token base
272	    int64_t ep_heap_stride_floats = 0;        // per-PE symmetric stride (floats)
273	    int     ep_team_local_pe      = 0;        // pe-in-EP-team (== ep_rank)
274	    int     ep_team_n_pes         = 1;        // EP team size  (== ep_size)

2	#define SG_FUSED_SM90_TP_TRANSPORT_CUH_
3	// ============================================================================
4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/tp_transport.cuh — the TENSOR-PARALLEL TRANSPORT SEAM.
5	//
6	// IMPLEMENTS: /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §5.2 (device-initiated all-reduce
7	// inside the persistent megakernel, FIXED-ORDER so the cross-rank A/A/A gate
8	// §6.4 holds) + §5.3/§5.4 (the transport go/no-go is an IMPLEMENTATION choice;
9	// the TP math is transport-agnostic). Authored 1-GPU/CPU per design §7; task #25
10	// phase-2 authoring (Lane C).
11	//
12	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
13	//  THE TRANSPORT SWAP POINT (read this first)
14	//
15	//  The TP all-reduce math (tp_layer.cuh) is written against ONE device-side
16	//  concept, `TpTransport`:
17	//
18	//      int     my_pe()  const            — this rank's index in the TP group
19	//      int     n_pes()  const            — TP group size
20	//      float*  local(int64_t off)        — THIS pe's buffer at symmetric offset
21	//      const float* peer(int64_t off,p)  — pe p's buffer at the SAME offset
22	//      (rendezvous)                      — the caller's GridBarrier + (real
23	//                                          multi-GPU only) the cross-GPU barrier
24	//                                          via Transport::rendezvous(bar)
25	//
26	//  TWO implementations live here:
27	//
28	//  * `LoopbackTransport` — the SINGLE-PROCESS, single-GPU loopback. The
29	//    "symmetric heap" is ONE device allocation of n_pes * stride floats; virtual
30	//    pe p's region is base + p*stride. All virtual PEs run in ONE grid (the CTAs
31	//    are partitioned into contiguous per-PE groups), so the cross-PE rendezvous
32	//    IS the existing GridBarrier over the whole grid. This is an HONEST
33	//    simulation: the TP math (shard GEMMs, partial publish, fixed-order
34	//    ascending-pe fp32 reduce) executes the IDENTICAL code path it executes on
35	//    NVSHMEM — the only thing swapped is (a) the symmetric-address translation
36	//    and (b) the rendezvous scope, which is precisely the transport abstraction.
37	//    It is NOT fake success: the loopback test (tests/hw/test_tp_loopback.py)
38	//    asserts bit-exact cross-virtual-rank identity + A/A/A + an exact-slice dW
39	//    check against the unsharded reference — failures fail loudly.
40	//
41	//  * `NvshmemTransport` — the REAL device-initiated NVSHMEM transport (design
42	//    §5.2). NVSHMEM IS NOT INSTALLED ON THIS BOX (verified 2026-06-12: no
43	//    headers/libs/pip/ldconfig hits), so this struct compiles ONLY under
44	//    -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1 with the NVSHMEM toolkit on the include/link path. It is
45	//    NOT a stub that pretends to work: without the flag it does not exist, and
46	//    any attempt to instantiate the megakernel TP point with it is a loud
47	//    compile error pointing here. Wiring + validating it is the ONE genuinely
48	//    8×H100 task (design §7.5) — swap `LoopbackTransport` → `NvshmemTransport`
49	//    at the call sites and run the §5.4 go/no-go gate.
50	//
51	//  WHY offset-based symmetric addressing (not raw pointers): NVSHMEM's
52	//  symmetric heap guarantees the SAME offset is valid on every PE
53	//  (nvshmem_malloc returns symmetric addresses; nvshmem_ptr(sym, pe) translates
54	//  for NVLink load/store). The loopback reproduces exactly that property with
55	//  base + pe*stride. One addressing model ⇒ one math code path.
56	//
57	//  DETERMINISM (design §5.2, non-negotiable): the fixed-order all-reduce below
58	//  reads every PE's partial in ASCENDING pe order and accumulates fp32. The
59	//  summation order is STRUCTURAL (never timing-dependent), so the result is
60	//  bit-identical on every PE and across reruns — the cross-rank analogue of the
61	//  in-kernel ascending-CTA reduce that made the single-GPU path A/A/A.
62	//  A `nvshmem_float_sum_reduce` collective is deliberately NOT used (its
63	//  reduction order is unspecified) — on NVSHMEM the same ascending-pe loop runs
64	//  over nvshmem_ptr-translated peer pointers (NVLink direct load/store).
65	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
66	//
67	// HEADER-ONLY, self-contained: CUDA runtime + the GridBarrier substrate only.
68	// No torch, no NCCL. Compiles for sm_90a with plain nvcc.
69	// ============================================================================
70

86	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
87	//  FORWARD DECLARATIONS of the sharded partial-GEMM helpers (DEFINED in
88	//  tp_layer.cuh — which includes model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh for the dectc_gemm_*
89	//  bodies). The decoder tile header (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh) includes THIS
90	//  header and references these by qualified name inside dectc_*_tile_impl, so
91	//  the first-phase name lookup needs the declarations here even though the
92	//  definitions land later in tp_layer.cuh (the include cycle: tp_layer →
93	//  model_stage_decoder_tc → tp_transport). Signatures MUST match tp_layer.cuh.
94	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
95	template <int N, class Transport, class WT>
96	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_rowparallel_fwd_partial_tile(
97	        const Transport& tr, int64_t slot_off,
98	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ Xown, const WT* __restrict__ Wshard,
99	        int Kin_local, int Nout,
100	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB);
101	template <int N, class Transport, class WT>
102	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_colparallel_dx_partial_tile(
103	        const Transport& tr, int64_t slot_off,
104	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ dYown, const WT* __restrict__ Wshard,
105	        int Kin, int Nout_local,
106	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB);

108	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
109	//  LoopbackTransport — single-process symmetric-heap simulation (the 1-GPU
110	//  honest test transport). See the swap-point doc above.
111	//
112	//  Host side: allocate ONE device buffer of `n_pes * stride_floats` floats and
113	//  pass (base, stride_floats, n_pes). Device side: each CTA derives its virtual
114	//  pe from its blockIdx (contiguous CTA groups per PE — `pe_of_cta`).
115	//  The rendezvous is the caller's whole-grid GridBarrier (all virtual PEs share
116	//  the grid), so `rendezvous()` simply forwards to bar.sync().
117	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
118	struct LoopbackTransport {
119	    float*  heap_base;       // [n_pes * stride_floats] device alloc
120	    int64_t stride_floats;   // per-PE symmetric region size
121	    int     n_pes_;          // TP degree being simulated
122	    int     my_pe_;          // this CTA-group's virtual rank
123	
124	    __device__ __forceinline__ int my_pe() const { return my_pe_; }
125	    __device__ __forceinline__ int n_pes() const { return n_pes_; }
126	
127	    // THIS pe's buffer at symmetric offset `off`.
128	    __device__ __forceinline__ float* local(int64_t off) const {
129	        return heap_base + (int64_t)my_pe_ * stride_floats + off;
130	    }
131	    // Peer pe's buffer at the SAME symmetric offset (ascending-pe reads in the
132	    // fixed-order reduce). On NVSHMEM this is nvshmem_ptr(sym, pe); here it is
133	    // the strided region — same contract, swapped translation.
134	    __device__ __forceinline__ const float* peer(int64_t off, int pe) const {
135	        return heap_base + (int64_t)pe * stride_floats + off;
136	    }
137	
138	    // Cross-PE rendezvous. Loopback: every virtual PE lives in THIS grid, so the
139	    // whole-grid GridBarrier IS the cross-PE barrier (publish partials → sync →
140	    // read peers → sync → reuse slots).
141	    __device__ __forceinline__ void rendezvous(const ::sg::fused::GridBarrier& bar) const {
142	        bar.sync();
143	    }
144	
145	    // Static CTA→PE partition helper: contiguous CTA groups (CTA c of nCTA, P
146	    // pes → pe = c / (nCTA/P); caller guarantees nCTA % P == 0, asserted in the
147	    // launchers). Contiguity keeps each virtual rank's tile traversal identical
148	    // to a real per-GPU grid (ascending tiles within the rank).
149	    __host__ __device__ __forceinline__ static int pe_of_cta(int cta, int nCTA, int P) {
150	        return cta / (nCTA / P);
151	    }
152	    __host__ __device__ __forceinline__ static int cta_within_pe(int cta, int nCTA, int P) {
153	        return cta % (nCTA / P);
154	    }
155	    __host__ __device__ __forceinline__ static int ctas_per_pe(int nCTA, int P) {
156	        return nCTA / P;
157	    }
158	};

160	#if defined(SG_HAS_NVSHMEM)
161	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
162	//  NvshmemTransport — the REAL device-initiated transport (design §5.2).
163	//  COMPILED ONLY under -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM=1 (NVSHMEM 3.7.0 IS installed:
164	//  NVSHMEM_HOME=/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/nvidia/nvshmem; the TU
165	//  that instantiates a kTPComm point must be built -rdc=true and device-linked
166	//  against libnvshmem_device_sm_90.bc — see /workspace/impl_diffs/tp_kernel.md
167	//  §6). The math code path is IDENTICAL to the loopback's; only the address
168	//  translation + the rendezvous scope differ:
169	//    * `heap_base` is an nvshmem_malloc'd SYMMETRIC allocation (same offset
170	//      valid on every PE) — a plain cudaMalloc pointer is NOT addressable via
171	//      nvshmem_ptr, so the TP slots MUST live on the symmetric heap the
172	//      launcher carves (tp_kernel.md §2/EDIT E). `tp_team_` is the TP-group
173	//      team (NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD when TP == world); `peer()` is called with the
174	//      TEAM-LOCAL pe and translated to the global pe for nvshmem_ptr.
175	//    * `peer()` translates via nvshmem_ptr (NVLink direct load/store — the
176	//      single-node 8×H100 case; a multi-node fabric would use nvshmem_get,
177	//      the documented extension point, NOT silently emulated);
178	//    * `rendezvous()` = in-GPU GridBarrier + nvshmem_quiet (drain THIS PE's
179	//      published partials so peers' NVLink loads see them) + ONE CTA running
180	//      the cross-GPU TEAM-scoped block barrier + GridBarrier again. The NVSHMEM
181	//      barrier is entered by exactly one CTA per GPU, NEVER concurrently with
182	//      the GridBarrier spin (the design's "two barrier systems must not
183	//      deadlock" rule, tp_nvshmem.md §1(3)).
184	//    * TEAM SCOPE: nvshmemx_barrier_block(tp_team_) joins ONLY the TP group, so
185	//      under a 4D mesh DP/PP replicas are not dragged into the TP barrier.
186	//      NVSHMEM 3.7.0 exposes nvshmemx_barrier_block (host/nvshmemx_coll_api.h:112),
187	//      so the tp_nvshmem.md §3.1 "version-dependent follow-up" is RESOLVED — no
188	//      whole-world fallback needed.
189	//  GO/NO-GO (§5.4): parity vs host-NCCL TP, A/A/A, MFU, ZeRO-3/DP composition.
190	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
191	struct NvshmemTransport {
192	    float*         heap_base;  // nvshmem_malloc'd symmetric base (LOCAL pointer)
193	    nvshmem_team_t tp_team_;   // the TP-group team (NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD if TP==world)
194	    int            n_pes_;     // TP group size  (nvshmem_team_n_pes(tp_team_))
195	    int            my_pe_;     // this GPU's pe-in-team (nvshmem_team_my_pe(tp_team_))
196	
197	    __device__ __forceinline__ int my_pe() const { return my_pe_; }
198	    __device__ __forceinline__ int n_pes() const { return n_pes_; }
199	
200	    __device__ __forceinline__ float* local(int64_t off) const {
201	        return heap_base + off;
202	    }
203	    __device__ __forceinline__ const float* peer(int64_t off, int pe_in_team) const {
204	        // peer() is called with the TEAM-LOCAL pe index (ascending 0..n_pes()-1,
205	        // the fixed reduce order); map it to the GLOBAL pe nvshmem_ptr needs.
206	        const int global_pe = nvshmem_team_translate_pe(tp_team_, pe_in_team,
207	                                                         NVSHMEM_TEAM_WORLD);
208	        return static_cast<const float*>(nvshmem_ptr(heap_base, global_pe)) + off;
209	    }
210	
211	    __device__ __forceinline__ void rendezvous(const ::sg::fused::GridBarrier& bar) const {
212	        bar.sync();                       // all CTAs of THIS GPU arrived
213	        if (blockIdx.x == 0) {            // one CTA crosses the GPU boundary
214	            // Drain THIS PE's outstanding symmetric stores so the ascending-pe
215	            // NVLink loads on every peer observe our published partial, THEN
216	            // join the TP-group barrier (team-scoped — not the whole world).
217	            nvshmem_quiet();
218	            nvshmemx_barrier_block(tp_team_);
219	        }
220	        bar.sync();                       // release every CTA after the cross-GPU join
221	    }
222	};
223	#endif  // SG_HAS_NVSHMEM
224	
225	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
226	//  tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order — THE all-reduce both transports share.
227	//
228	//  PRE: every PE has PUBLISHED its fp32 partial at symmetric offset `slot_off`
229	//  (length n) and the caller has crossed `tr.rendezvous(bar)` once (so all
230	//  publishes are visible). POST: `dst[i] = Σ_pe partial_pe[i]`, summed in
231	//  ASCENDING pe order in fp32 — bit-identical on every PE and across reruns
232	//  (design §5.2/§2.7: structural order, the A/A/A non-negotiable). The caller
233	//  crosses `tr.rendezvous(bar)` again before REUSING the slot.
234	//
235	//  `tid`/`nthreads` define this PE's cooperative element loop. In the loopback
236	//  every virtual PE redundantly computes its own copy (each PE strides its own
237	//  CTA group's threads) — exactly what real per-GPU ranks do.
238	//
239	//  This is deliberately NOT nvshmem_float_sum_reduce: that collective's
240	//  reduction order is unspecified ⇒ ULP drift run-to-run ⇒ A/A/A failure
241	//  (design §5.2). The hand-rolled ascending-pe loop IS the deliverable.
242	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
243	template <class Transport>
244	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order(
245	        const Transport& tr, int64_t slot_off, float* __restrict__ dst,
246	        int64_t n, int tid, int nthreads) {
247	    const int P = tr.n_pes();
248	    for (int64_t i = tid; i < n; i += nthreads) {
249	        float acc = 0.0f;
250	        #pragma unroll 1
251	        for (int pe = 0; pe < P; ++pe) {        // ASCENDING pe — fixed order
252	            acc += tr.peer(slot_off, pe)[i];
253	        }
254	        dst[i] = acc;
255	    }
256	}
257	
258	// Variant writing the reduced value back INTO this PE's symmetric slot (in-place
259	// consumers); same fixed order. Safe because every PE reads ALL peers before any
260	// PE can pass the post-reduce rendezvous the caller crosses before reuse — the
261	// read-before-overwrite hazard is what that second rendezvous exists for, so
262	// this variant must write to a DIFFERENT slot than it reads. Kept explicit:
263	template <class Transport>
264	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order_to_slot(
265	        const Transport& tr, int64_t src_slot_off, int64_t dst_slot_off,
266	        int64_t n, int tid, int nthreads) {
267	    float* dst = tr.local(dst_slot_off);
268	    tp_allreduce_sum_fixed_order(tr, src_slot_off, dst, n, tid, nthreads);
269	}
270	
271	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
272	//  make_transport_from_comm<Par> — the ONE place that selects the transport
273	//  from a populated par::CommCtx, so the megakernel constructs `tr` with a
274	//  single call (no #if clutter at the call site). Returns:
275	//    * NvshmemTransport       when -DSG_HAS_NVSHMEM (the real 8×H100 path),
276	//    * LoopbackTransport      otherwise (the single-GPU honest simulation).
277	//  Both read the SAME CommCtx fields (sym-heap base, stride, team pe/size), so
278	//  the launcher populates ONE struct and either transport binds it. Only ever
279	//  called under `if constexpr (Par::kTPComm)` (folded away on SingleGPU), so it
280	//  is never instantiated on the byte-identical default path.
281	//
282	//  The CommCtx type is forward-declared opaquely here to avoid pulling
283	//  parallel_config.cuh's include into every tp_transport.cuh consumer; the real
284	//  definition (par::CommCtx) is included by the megakernel before this is used.
285	//  The fields read are POD (float*/int64_t/int) — no NVSHMEM type crosses the
286	//  CommCtx boundary (the team handle is a void* cast to nvshmem_team_t here).
287	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
288	template <class Par, class CommT>
289	__device__ __forceinline__ auto make_transport_from_comm(const CommT& comm) {
290	#if defined(SG_HAS_NVSHMEM)
291	    return NvshmemTransport{
292	        reinterpret_cast<float*>(comm.tp_sym_heap),
293	        static_cast<nvshmem_team_t>(reinterpret_cast<intptr_t>(comm.tp_comm_handle)),
294	        comm.tp_team_n_pes, comm.tp_team_local_pe };
295	#else
296	    return LoopbackTransport{
297	        reinterpret_cast<float*>(comm.tp_sym_heap), comm.tp_heap_stride_floats,
298	        comm.tp_team_n_pes, comm.tp_team_local_pe };
299	#endif
300	}

4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/tp_layer.cuh — TENSOR-PARALLEL math for the L3-TC decoder
5	// megakernel: the Megatron column/row split geometry, the sharded wgmma tile
6	// GEMMs, and the two in-step all-reduce points.
7	//
8	// IMPLEMENTS: /workspace/.parallelism_design.md §5.1 (where the all-reduce
9	// lands — col-parallel in_proj/ff0, row-parallel out_proj/ff2, TWO all-reduces
10	// per layer) + §5.2 (fixed-order in-kernel reduce, via tp_transport.cuh).
11	// Authored 1-GPU per design §7 (task #25 phase-2, Lane C). The TP MATH here is
12	// the durable deliverable; the transport behind it is the swap point
13	// (tp_transport.cuh — loopback now, NVSHMEM at the 8× window).
14	//
15	// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
16	//  THE MEGATRON SPLIT ON THIS KERNEL'S WEIGHT LAYOUT (all row-major [Nout,Kin],
17	//  matching DecWeights / decoder_layout.cuh):
18	//

98	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
99	//  Shard geometry. Contiguous block ownership along the split dimension; the
100	//  TP degree must divide the split extents AND keep heads whole (static checks
101	//  where compile-time, runtime asserts in the host plan otherwise).
102	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
103	enum class TpSplit : int8_t {
104	    Replicated = 0,   // full tensor on every rank (grads bit-identical, no comm)
105	    Col        = 1,   // split along Nout (output features) — rank owns a row block
106	    Row        = 2,   // split along Kin (input features)   — rank owns a col block
107	    ColQKV     = 3,   // in_proj 3-block column split (q|k|v each split by heads)
108	};
109	
110	struct TpTensorShard { int tidx; TpSplit split; };

112	// The 30-tensor decoder shard table (dec_layout named_parameters() order — the
113	// single source decoder_layout.cuh mirrors). See the header table.
114	constexpr int kDecTpNumTensors = 30;
115	__device__ __constant__ TpTensorShard kDecTpShard[kDecTpNumTensors] = {
116	    { 0, TpSplit::Replicated},  // tok.weight
117	    { 1, TpSplit::Replicated},  // pos.weight
118	    { 2, TpSplit::ColQKV    },  // L0 in_proj_weight
119	    { 3, TpSplit::ColQKV    },  // L0 in_proj_bias
120	    { 4, TpSplit::Row       },  // L0 out_proj.weight
121	    { 5, TpSplit::Replicated},  // L0 out_proj.bias  (post-reduce add)
122	    { 6, TpSplit::Replicated},  // L0 n1.weight
123	    { 7, TpSplit::Replicated},  // L0 n1.bias
124	    { 8, TpSplit::Replicated},  // L0 n2.weight

148	// Contiguous own-range along a split extent. Requires P | extent (TP degrees
149	// are powers of two and d/dff/3d at every ladder width are multiples of 8·64;
150	// the host plan asserts before launch — no silent remainder handling).
151	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ void tp_own_range(
152	        int extent, int P, int r, int* lo, int* hi) {
153	    const int per = extent / P;     // caller asserts extent % P == 0
154	    *lo = r * per;
155	    *hi = *lo + per;
156	}
157	
158	// Heads-per-rank for the QKV/head-aligned splits. Requires P | H so each rank's
159	// column block is whole heads (the local attention precondition).
160	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int tp_heads_per_rank(int H, int P) {
161	    return H / P;                   // caller asserts H % P == 0
162	}
163	
164	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
165	//  Host-side dense shard packing maps (how a rank STORES its shard). The rank
166	//  keeps its shard DENSE — [Nout/P, Kin] for Col, [Nout, Kin/P] for Row, and
167	//  for ColQKV the q|k|v own-blocks concatenated [3·d/P, d] — so every sharded
168	//  GEMM below reads it exactly like the unsharded kernel reads a full weight
169	//  (row-major, no strides). These index helpers define the pack ONCE (host
170	//  packers + tests both call them; no duplicated arithmetic).
171	//    Col   : dense row i  ↔ full row (own_lo + i)
172	//    Row   : dense col j  ↔ full col (own_lo + j)
173	//    ColQKV: dense row i  ↔ full row (block(i)·d + own_lo + i % (d/P)),
174	//            block(i) = i / (d/P) ∈ {0,1,2} = {q,k,v}
175	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
176	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int tp_col_full_row(int own_lo, int i) {
177	    return own_lo + i;
178	}
179	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int tp_row_full_col(int own_lo, int j) {
180	    return own_lo + j;
181	}
182	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int tp_colqkv_full_row(int d, int P, int r, int i) {
183	    const int per = d / P;          // rows per (q|k|v) block on one rank
184	    const int blk = i / per;        // 0=q, 1=k, 2=v
185	    const int off = i % per;
186	    return blk * d + r * per + off;
187	}
188	
189	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
190	//  THE PER-TILE TP BLOCK FUNCTIONS (the megakernel-tiling math). All reuse the
191	//  PRODUCTION wgmma tile GEMMs (dectc_gemm_fwd_f32 / dectc_gemm_dx_f32 — fp32
192	//  accumulate, kTileM=128-row tiles, identical staging) on the rank's DENSE
193	//  shard; zero new GEMM math. `Wshard` is templated on the weight dtype (WT):
194	//  the loopback test passes fp32 params (const float*, the fp32→bf16-on-read
195	//  GEMM overload); the production megakernel passes the PRECONVERTED bf16 cache
196	//  (const __nv_bfloat16*, DecWBf::*). dectc_gemm_fwd_f32/_dx_f32 overload on the
197	//  W pointer type, so the right body is selected automatically for each caller.
198	//
199	//  COLUMN-parallel forward:  Y_own[M, Nout/P] = X[M,Kin] @ Wshard^T.
200	//  Comm-free; the output IS the rank's feature shard.
201	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
202	template <int N, class WT>
203	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_colparallel_fwd_tile(
204	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ X, const WT* __restrict__ Wshard,
205	        float* __restrict__ Yown, int Kin, int Nout_local,
206	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB) {
207	    dectc::dectc_gemm_fwd_f32<N>(X, Wshard, Yown, Kin, Nout_local, sA, sB);
208	}
209	
210	// ROW-parallel forward PARTIAL: Ypart[M, Nout] = X_own[M, Kin/P] @ Wshard^T,
211	// written DIRECTLY into this PE's symmetric slot (the publish). The caller then
212	// crosses the rendezvous and runs the fixed-order reduce (all-reduce point ①/②).
213	template <int N, class Transport, class WT>
214	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_rowparallel_fwd_partial_tile(
215	        const Transport& tr, int64_t slot_off,
216	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ Xown, const WT* __restrict__ Wshard,
217	        int Kin_local, int Nout,
218	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB) {
219	    dectc::dectc_gemm_fwd_f32<N>(Xown, Wshard, tr.local(slot_off),
220	                                 Kin_local, Nout, sA, sB);
221	}
222	
223	// ROW-parallel backward dX (comm-free): dXown[M, Kin/P] = dY[M, Nout] @ Wshard.
224	// dY is the FULL-width adjoint (the row-parallel output was all-reduced, so its
225	// adjoint is replicated); Wshard is the rank's [Nout, Kin/P] dense col-shard.
226	template <int N, class WT>
227	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_rowparallel_dx_tile(
228	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ dY, const WT* __restrict__ Wshard,
229	        float* __restrict__ dXown, int Kin_local, int Nout,
230	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB) {
231	    dectc::dectc_gemm_dx_f32<N>(dY, Wshard, dXown, Kin_local, Nout, sA, sB);
232	}
233	
234	// COLUMN-parallel backward dX PARTIAL (the conjugate comm point ①'/②'):
235	// dXpart[M, Kin] = dYown[M, Nout/P] @ Wshard, published to the symmetric slot;
236	// caller rendezvous + fixed-order reduce ⇒ dX = Σ_pe dXpart.
237	template <int N, class Transport, class WT>
238	__device__ __forceinline__ void tp_colparallel_dx_partial_tile(
239	        const Transport& tr, int64_t slot_off,
240	        const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ dYown, const WT* __restrict__ Wshard,
241	        int Kin, int Nout_local,
242	        __nv_bfloat16* sA, __nv_bfloat16* sB) {
243	    dectc::dectc_gemm_dx_f32<N>(dYown, Wshard, tr.local(slot_off),
244	                                Kin, Nout_local, sA, sB);
245	}
246	
247	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
248	//  dW under TP — the exact-slice property (NO comm, the P2 machinery carries
249	//  over unchanged). For a COLUMN-parallel weight, the rank's
250	//      dW_own[Nout/P, Kin] = dY_own^T @ X        (X full/replicated)
251	//  is bit-for-bit rows [own_lo, own_hi) of the unsharded dW (same ascending-K
252	//  fp32 contraction over the same T). For a ROW-parallel weight,
253	//      dW_own[Nout, Kin/P] = dY^T @ X_own        (dY full/replicated)
254	//  is bit-for-bit cols [own_lo, own_hi). So P2's output-stationary dW spec for
255	//  a TP rank is the SAME DecDwSpec with (dY, Nout) or (X, Kin) swapped for the
256	//  rank-local stream/extent — this helper performs that transform. Biases:
257	//  col-parallel db_own = Σ_K dY_own (the own rows of db); row-parallel /
258	//  replicated db = Σ_K dY computed identically on every rank.
259	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
260	__device__ __host__ __forceinline__ void tp_shard_extents(
261	        TpSplit split, int P, int Nout_full, int Kin_full,
262	        int* Nout_local, int* Kin_local) {
263	    switch (split) {
264	        case TpSplit::Col:
265	        case TpSplit::ColQKV: *Nout_local = Nout_full / P; *Kin_local = Kin_full;     break;
266	        case TpSplit::Row:    *Nout_local = Nout_full;     *Kin_local = Kin_full / P; break;
267	        default:              *Nout_local = Nout_full;     *Kin_local = Kin_full;     break;
268	    }
269	}
270	
271	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
272	//  Symmetric-slot budget for one decoder layer's TP comm, in floats, per tile
273	//  row block of kTileM rows: the largest reduced payload is [kTileM, d] (both
274	//  fwd reduces and both bwd reduces are [rows, d]). The canonical heap plan
275	//  (the loopback binding + the future NVSHMEM bootstrap both size with this):
276	//      slot 0: partial  [kTileM · d]      (publish target)
277	//      slot 1: reduced  [kTileM · d]      (reduce output, when not fused into
278	//                                          a local consumer buffer)
279	//  per CONCURRENT tile in flight per PE. The persistent kernel runs ONE tile
280	//  per CTA at a time ⇒ heap stride = n_ctas_per_pe · 2 · kTileM · d floats.
281	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
282	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t tp_tile_slot_floats() {
283	    return (int64_t)dectc::kTileM * dec::kD;
284	}
285	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t tp_heap_stride_floats(int ctas_per_pe) {
286	    return (int64_t)ctas_per_pe * 2 * tp_tile_slot_floats();
287	}
288	
289	}}}}  // namespace sg::fused::sm90::tp
290	
291	#endif  // SG_FUSED_SM90_TP_LAYER_CUH_

144	// Rebase a FusedOptState's per-element state pointers to a parameter-tensor
145	// slice at `off` within the flat [m|v|extra] layout. Per-TENSOR fields (the
146	// NeuralGrok psi MLP weights) and all scalars pass through unchanged.
147	template <OptId Opt>
148	__device__ __forceinline__ FusedOptState
149	rebase_state(const FusedOptState& s, int64_t off) {
150	    FusedOptState t = s;  // scalars + per-tensor pointers copy as-is
151	    if (t.exp_avg)    t.exp_avg    += off;
152	    if (t.exp_avg_sq) t.exp_avg_sq += off;
153	    if (t.ema)        t.ema        += off;
154	    if (t.sam_dir)    t.sam_dir    += off;
155	    if (t.s_track)    t.s_track    += off;
156	    if (t.mu)         t.mu         += off;
157	    if (t.orth)       t.orth       += off;
158	    if (t.smart_grad) t.smart_grad += off;
159	    if (t.param_init) t.param_init += off;   // Prodigy trajectory anchor p0
160	    if (t.sharpness)  t.sharpness  += off;   // SuperGrok11/15 (g_sam−g)² (per element)
161	    // SuperGrok11/15 phi weights (sg_phi_W1/b1/W2) are a per-TENSOR weight SET (same
162	    // for every element), NOT a per-element slice — so they are NOT rebased (the same
163	    // pointer is staged to SMEM once per block, exactly like NeuralGrok's psi pointers).
164	    return t;
165	}

167	// The L3-REAL decoder megakernel needs the token path + a grad-partial workspace
168	// in addition to the FuseTier::{L1,L3} ABI. We keep it a SEPARATE kernel +
169	// launcher (not folded into fused_megakernel) so the surrogate path is untouched.
170	//
171	// Workspace layout (one flat float buffer the host allocates + the kernel owns):
172	//   [0 .. nCTA*total)              : per-CTA grad partials (cta-major)
173	//   [nCTA*total .. nCTA*total+nCTA): per-CTA loss partials (NLL sum per slice)
174	//   [.. +1)                        : the reduced scalar loss (loss/B) the host reads
175	// total == kDecTotalElems == 422755.
176	
177	struct DecoderTokenCtx {
178	    const int* tokens;   // [B, kSeq] int32 token ids in [0, kVocab)
179	    const int* targets;  // [B]       int32 target ids
180	    int        B;        // batch size (full-batch in the race ≈ 4191)
181	    float*     workspace; // grad partials + loss partials + reduced loss
182	    float*     loss_out;  // device float the kernel writes the mean loss into
183	};

185	#if SG_DEC_SCALAR_MEGAKERNEL
186	// ── The persistent megakernel (L3-REAL). gridDim.x = #SMs (one CTA/SM), 256
187	//    threads/CTA. The smem holds ONE DecSampleSmem (≈42 KB, < 48 KB static cap —
188	//    no dynamic-smem opt-in, so the occupancy≥1 guard with dynamicSMemBytes=0 in
189	//    the launcher is unchanged). ────────────────────────────────────────────────
190	//    GATED by SG_DEC_SCALAR_MEGAKERNEL (this legacy fp32 path's DecSampleSmem
191	//    grows with SG_DEC_D and ptxas-fails at large d; OFF lets the TC path build
192	//    at scaled d — see the flag note above). ────────────────────────────────────
193	// sizes/offsets are NOT host-passed: the per-tensor numel/offset live in the
194	// generated __constant__ tables kDecSizes/kDecOffsets (decoder_layout.cuh), so
195	// the reduce + optimizer phases read them directly. This also lets the host side
196	// (dispatch.cpp) avoid building any layout tensors.
197	template <OptId Opt>
198	__global__ void __launch_bounds__(SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK)
199	fused_decoder_megakernel(PersistentContext ctx,
200	                         float* __restrict__ params,
201	                         DecoderTokenCtx tok,
202	                         float* __restrict__ grad,        // reduced grad [total]
203	                         float lr, int step, FusedOptState st) {
204	    __shared__ DecSampleSmem sm;
205	    GridBarrier bar = ctx.barrier();
206	    const int cta = blockIdx.x;
207	    const int nCTA = (int)ctx.n_ctas;
208	    const int64_t total = kDecTotalElems;
209	    float* my_partial = tok.workspace + (int64_t)cta * total;   // this CTA's dW
210	    float* loss_part = tok.workspace + (int64_t)nCTA * total;   // [nCTA]
211	
212	    // §3.4 register repartition (producer WG gives back, consumer WG claims).
213	    const int wg = threadIdx.x / 128;
214	    // warp-specialize prims live in sg::sm90::wgs (this file is sg::fused::sm90)
215	    if (wg == 0) ::sg::sm90::wgs::warpgroup_reg_dealloc<32>();
216	    else         ::sg::sm90::wgs::warpgroup_reg_alloc<200>();
217	
218	    // ── P0: zero this CTA's grad-partial slice + its loss slot. ───────────────
219	    for (int64_t i = threadIdx.x; i < total; i += blockDim.x) my_partial[i] = 0.0f;
220	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) loss_part[cta] = 0.0f;
221	    bar.sync();   // B0
222	
223	    // ── P1: batch-parallel fwd+bwd. Fixed contiguous slice [b0,b1) for this CTA.
224	    DecWeights w = dec_bind(params);
225	    DecGrad g = dec_bind_grad(my_partial);
226	    // Even split with remainder to the low CTAs (contiguous, deterministic).
227	    const int B = tok.B;
228	    const int base = B / nCTA, rem = B % nCTA;
229	    const int b0 = cta * base + (cta < rem ? cta : rem);
230	    const int cnt = base + (cta < rem ? 1 : 0);
231	    const int b1 = b0 + cnt;
232	    __shared__ int tok_s[dec::kSeq];   // this sample's token ids (broadcast)
233	    __shared__ int tgt_s;
234	    float nll_acc = 0.0f;              // fp32 slice accumulator (thread-0 holds it)
235	    for (int b = b0; b < b1; ++b) {
236	        if (threadIdx.x < dec::kSeq) tok_s[threadIdx.x] = tok.tokens[(int64_t)b * dec::kSeq + threadIdx.x];
237	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) tgt_s = tok.targets[b];
238	        __syncthreads();
239	        float nll = dec_forward_sample(w, tok_s, tgt_s, &sm);
240	        dec_backward_sample(w, g, tok_s, tgt_s, B, &sm);
241	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) nll_acc += nll;   // fixed-order fp32 sum within slice
242	        __syncthreads();   // sample boundary: all grad writes done before reuse
243	    }
244	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) loss_part[cta] = nll_acc;
245	    bar.sync();   // B1: all CTA partials + loss slots complete
246	
247	    // ── P2: deterministic cross-CTA reduce. Work-steal the param ELEMENT-RANGES
248	    //    (one task = one parameter tensor; sum its elements across CTAs in
249	    //    ascending CTA index). The summation ORDER (ascending cta) is fixed, so
250	    //    the result is deterministic regardless of which CTA grabs the task. ────
251	    {
252	        __shared__ int task_slot;
253	        TaskQueue q = ctx.queue();
254	        for (int t = q.next_block(&task_slot); t < kDecNumTensors;
255	             t = q.next_block(&task_slot)) {
256	            const int n = kDecSizes[t];
257	            const int64_t off = (int64_t)kDecOffsets[t];
258	            for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < n; i += blockDim.x) {
259	                float acc = 0.0f;
260	                // ascending CTA index → fixed fp32 summation order (deterministic).
261	                for (int c = 0; c < nCTA; ++c)
262	                    acc += tok.workspace[(int64_t)c * total + off + i];
263	                grad[off + i] = acc;
264	            }
265	        }
266	    }
267	    // Loss reduction (fp64 ordered) by CTA 0 only — the 1e-5 loss rel-tol is the
268	    // tightest gate; fp32 atomic-summing ~4191 terms can miss it.
269	    if (cta == 0 && threadIdx.x == 0) {
270	        double s = 0.0;
271	        for (int c = 0; c < nCTA; ++c) s += (double)loss_part[c];
272	        float mean = (float)(s / (double)B);
273	        *tok.loss_out = mean;
274	    }
275	    bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task);   // B2: reduced grad ready; reset queue for P3
276	
277	    // ── P3: the REAL optimizer tail over the reduced grad (work-steal the 30
278	    //    tensors). apply_optimizer<Opt> is the canonical csrc/algorithms math. ──
279	    st.lr = lr;
280	    {
281	        __shared__ int task_slot;
282	        TaskQueue q = ctx.queue();
283	        for (int t = q.next_block(&task_slot); t < kDecNumTensors;
284	             t = q.next_block(&task_slot)) {
285	            const int n = kDecSizes[t];
286	            const int64_t off = (int64_t)kDecOffsets[t];
287	            const FusedOptState ts = rebase_state<Opt>(st, off);
288	            float* __restrict__ p = params + off;
289	            const float* __restrict__ gg = grad + off;
290	            for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < n; i += blockDim.x)
291	                apply_optimizer<Opt>(p, gg, (int64_t)i, step, ts);
292	        }
293	    }
294	}

296	// ── Host launcher — one persistent CTA per SM, 256 threads/CTA (2 warp-groups).
297	//    Mirrors launch_fused_megakernel's hang-freedom contract: occupancy≥1 or
298	//    refuse (the GridBarrier rendezvous of n_ctas CTAs can never complete if a
299	//    CTA can't be placed). Zeroes the barrier+task counters per launch. ─────────
300	template <OptId Opt>
301	cudaError_t launch_fused_decoder_megakernel(
302	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params, DecoderTokenCtx tok,
303	        float* grad, float lr, int step, FusedOptState st, cudaStream_t stream) {
304	    int dev = 0;
305	    cudaError_t err = cudaGetDevice(&dev);
306	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
307	    int n_sms = 0;
308	    err = cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&n_sms, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, dev);
309	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
310	
311	    int occ = 0;
312	    err = cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(
313	        &occ, (const void*)&fused_decoder_megakernel<Opt>, SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK,
314	        /*dynamicSMemBytes=*/0);
315	    if (err != cudaSuccess) return err;
316	    // Hang-freedom: at least one CTA per SM must be resident or the grid barrier
317	    // can never be satisfied. The L3-REAL kernel uses ≈42 KB static smem + a high
318	    // register count; if it cannot place one block/SM, REFUSE rather than hang.
319	    assert(occ >= 1 &&
320	           "fused_decoder_megakernel: 0 blocks/SM — GridBarrier would hang. The "
321	           "decoder smem (~42KB) + regs exceed one-block-per-SM occupancy; "
322	           "reduce footprint or fall back to the L1 per-op path.");
323	    if (occ < 1) return cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources;
324	
325	    const unsigned launch_ctas = (unsigned)n_sms;
326	    ctx.n_ctas = launch_ctas;
327	
328	    if (ctx.g_arrived) { err = cudaMemsetAsync(ctx.g_arrived, 0, sizeof(unsigned), stream); if (err) return err; }
329	    if (ctx.g_generation) { err = cudaMemsetAsync(ctx.g_generation, 0, sizeof(unsigned), stream); if (err) return err; }
330	    if (ctx.g_next_task) { err = cudaMemsetAsync(ctx.g_next_task, 0, sizeof(int), stream); if (err) return err; }
331	
332	    dim3 grid(launch_ctas), block(SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK);
333	    fused_decoder_megakernel<Opt><<<grid, block, 0, stream>>>(
334	        ctx, params, tok, grad, lr, step, st);
335	    return cudaGetLastError();
336	}

345	// TC megakernel threads: 256 (the engine's producer+consumer warpgroup layout;
346	// wgmma is warpgroup-scoped on threads 0..127). We do NOT apply the scalar
347	// path's asymmetric setmaxnreg (dealloc<32> on WG0) — that would STARVE the MMA
348	// warpgroup (WG0 issues the wgmma; a 128-wide accumulator needs 64 fp32 regs/
349	// thread). The validated selftest ran no split; we match it.
350	#define SG_TC_MEGA_BLOCK 256

352	// ── smem arena for the unpipelined engine: one A(64×16) + one B(N×16) bf16 tile
353	//    + the 256-float reduction slot. 16B-aligned. N = SG_TUNED_TILE_N. The 9 dW
354	//    specs live here too (identical for all threads → shared, not per-thread
355	//    stack: keeps the launch's local-memory reservation small so the persistent
356	//    kernel places on a memory-tight GPU). ──
357	struct DecTcSmem {
358	    // GEMM K-loop ring. The M-atom-interleaved wgmma pipeline stages up to
359	    // kDecAtomsPerSlot A(64×16) tiles per slot (one per stacked m64 atom in an
360	    // interleave GROUP, issued back-to-back into independent fp32 fragments so the
361	    // tensor pipe overlaps them) + ONE shared B(N×16) tile per slot. Layout:
362	    // A-tiles packed [slot][atom-in-group] (slot s, atom ai at
363	    // sA + (s*kDecAtomsPerSlot + ai)*64*16); B [slot] at sB + s*N*16.
364	    // kDecAtomsPerSlot = min(kAtomsM, kDecMaxIL) = the widest interleave group any
365	    // call site uses (fwd/dX = kAtomsM=2; dW = 1). At S=2, =2, N=128 the ring is
366	    // 2·(2·2KB + 4KB)=16KB; DecTcSmem total ~17.5KB ≪ the 48KB static cap.
367	    static constexpr int kDecAtomsPerSlot =
368	        (dectc::kAtomsM < dectc::kDecMaxIL) ? dectc::kAtomsM : dectc::kDecMaxIL;
369	    // RING DEPTH for the smem allocation = kDecRingStagesMax = max(fwd/dX ring
370	    // depth, dW ring depth). When SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_PIPE=0 this == kDecTcStages
371	    // (the shipped 2), so sA/sB are BYTE-IDENTICAL to every shipped build → the
372	    // kernel's static smem (and thus the launcher's cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocks
373	    // certification) is unchanged. When PIPE=1 the deeper fwd/dX ring needs
374	    // kDecFwdStages (2..4) slots, so the ring smem grows ∝ depth — this is the
375	    // OCCUPANCY COST of the lever: at N=128, IL=2, each extra slot adds
376	    // (2·64·16 + 128·16)·2 B = 8 KB (sA +4KB, sB +4KB). The launcher REFUSES
377	    // (cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources) if the larger static smem drops occupancy
378	    // below 1 CTA/SM (the persistent grid-barrier requires ≥1) — so the operator
379	    // backs off the depth knob if a chosen depth won't place. NO register growth
380	    // (the WgmmaAccum<N> fragments are independent of ring depth), so the ceiling
381	    // is purely the 228 KB/SM smem budget (≈ depth 4 fits comfortably at d=2048).
382	    static constexpr int kDecRingStages = dectc::kDecRingStagesMax;
383	    // alignas(16): the cp.async RING (fwd/dX staging) lands 16-byte LDGSTS
384	    // chunks here, which require a 16B-aligned smem destination. Every
385	    // tile-internal offset is a multiple of 8 bf16 (16B) and the sA block size
386	    // is a multiple of 16B at every legal (stages, IL, TILE_N), so the alignas
387	    // changes NO member offset — it only pins the guarantee the ring needs.
388	    alignas(16) __nv_bfloat16 sA[kDecRingStages * kDecAtomsPerSlot * 64 * 16];
389	    alignas(16) __nv_bfloat16 sB[kDecRingStages * SG_TUNED_TILE_N * 16];
390	    float red[256];
391	    dectc::DecDwSpec spec[dectc::kDecNumDwSpecs];
392	#if SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_PIPE == 2
393	    // ── DESIGN-TOURNAMENT entry (b): producer/consumer mbarrier words for the
394	    //    PIPE=2 fwd/dX engine (tile_pipeline.cuh's full[]+empty[] ring). Two 8-byte
395	    //    barriers per stage (a "full" the producer arrives + an "empty" the consumer
396	    //    releases), Depth = kDecRingStages stages → 2·Depth words. This member is
397	    //    #if-GATED on the MACRO (not a constexpr), so on the shipped PIPE=0|1 builds
398	    //    it is ENTIRELY ABSENT — sizeof(DecTcSmem), the kernel's `.shared` PTX, and
399	    //    the launcher's static-smem occupancy cert are BYTE-IDENTICAL to every
400	    //    shipped build (PTX-proven OFF below). At PIPE=2 it adds 2·Depth·8 ≤ 64 B
401	    //    (Depth ≤ 4) on top of the deeper ring's sA/sB — negligible vs entry (a)'s
402	    //    SAME ring tiles (the occupancy ceiling is the depth-scaled sA/sB, identical
403	    //    for PIPE 1 vs 2; see kDecRingStagesMax). alignas(8): mbarrier words are
404	    //    8-byte; the array follows `spec` (8-byte-aligned members) → no prior member
405	    //    offset moves. The whole arena still fits the 48 KB STATIC cap at the
406	    //    default Depth (=2): sizeof ≈ 18.1 KB at d=128, ≈ 50.5 KB at d=2048/Depth=4
407	    //    — the launcher's cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocks≥1 cert REFUSES any depth that
408	    //    won't place at 1 CTA/SM (no forced launch); see launch_..._tc.
409	    alignas(8) unsigned long long pipe_bars[2 * kDecRingStages];
410	#endif
411	};

413	// ── DESIGN-TOURNAMENT entry (b): the fwd/dX tile-call trailing arg that hands the
414	//    producer/consumer engine its mbarrier words. Expands to `, sm.pipe_bars` ONLY
415	//    under PIPE=2 and to NOTHING otherwise — so the shipped PIPE=0|1 fwd/bwd tile
416	//    calls are TEXTUALLY UNCHANGED (the tile functions' `pipeBars` param defaults to
417	//    nullptr, unreferenced in their non-engine path → byte-identical PTX). Mirrors
418	//    the SG_DEC_FINE_* macro idiom. `sm` is the kernel's __shared__ DecTcSmem local;
419	//    this macro is only ever used inside fused_decoder_megakernel_tc where `sm` is
420	//    in scope. The dW + optimizer-tail calls do NOT take it (dW never enters the
421	//    ring; the tail has no GEMM) — only the 4 fwd/bwd tile call sites use it.
422	#if SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_PIPE == 2
423	#define SG_DEC_PIPE_BARS_ARG , sm.pipe_bars
424	#else
425	#define SG_DEC_PIPE_BARS_ARG
426	#endif

428	// ── DEEP-RING SMEM ALLOCATION GATE (decoder fwd/dX deeper-ring lever) ─────────
429	// The static __shared__ DecTcSmem (kernel `sm`, below) is hard-capped at 48 KB on

61	## §1 — THE LOAD-BEARING ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINT (the honest blocker the naïve plan misses)
62	
63	`tp_nvshmem.md §5.3` and `tp_layer.cuh`'s header say "wrap each of the four
64	reduce points in `if constexpr (Par::kTPComm)` and call `tr.rendezvous(bar)`".
65	That is correct ONLY at a grid-synchronized point. The production P1 loop is NOT
66	one. Verified live (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:840`):
67	
68	```cpp
69	    for (int ti = cta; ti < n_tiles; ti += nCTA) {            // GRID-STRIDE: each CTA
70	        const int g0 = ti * nrows_tile;                       // does a DIFFERENT count
71	        ...                                                    // of tiles
72	        nll = dectc::dectc_forward_tile(...);                 // ← reduce point ①/② live here
73	        dectc::dectc_backward_tile(...);                      // ← reduce point ①'/②' live here
74	    }
75	    ...
76	    bar.sync();   // B1   ← the FIRST grid barrier after P1
77	```
78	
79	`bar` is `GridBarrier` over `ctx.n_ctas` (`megakernel_common.cuh:147`): its
80	`sync()` waits for **every** launched CTA. If a `tr.rendezvous(bar)` (which calls
81	`bar.sync()`) is placed INSIDE the per-tile loop, CTA `c` reaches it
82	`ceil((n_tiles-c)/nCTA)` times while CTA `c'` reaches it a different number of
83	times ⇒ the arrival count never equals `n_ctas` on a given generation ⇒ **deadlock**.
84	The loopback test (`tp_loopback_binding.cu:93`) sidesteps this by launching
85	exactly `grid = P` CTAs with **one tile in flight per PE** (no grid-stride) — so
86	its whole-grid `bar.sync()` IS a clean rendezvous. That is the persistent-kernel
87	shape `tp_layer.cuh` documents ("one tile in flight per PE").
88	
89	**⇒ On the `kTPComm` path the P1 tile loop must be GRID-LOCKSTEP: all CTAs on a
90	GPU process the SAME tile index together, with `tr.rendezvous(bar)` at the four
91	reduce points being a barrier every CTA reaches the SAME number of times.** Two
92	sub-cases, both spelled out in EDIT C.3:
93	
94	- **TP-only single-GPU loopback (the bring-up gate, `LoopbackTransport`):** the
95	  virtual PEs share ONE grid; CTAs are partitioned into `P` contiguous per-PE
96	  groups (`LoopbackTransport::pe_of_cta`). Within a PE group the CTAs that own a
97	  tile still must reach the rendezvous in lockstep — so the loop is restructured
98	  to `for (tile_round = 0; tile_round < n_rounds; ++tile_round)` where every CTA
99	  participates in each round's rendezvous even if its PE has no row in that round
100	  (it publishes a zero-length partial / skips the GEMM but STILL calls
101	  `tr.rendezvous(bar)`). `n_rounds = ceil(n_tiles_per_pe)` is a GRID-UNIFORM
102	  count (all PEs have the same tile count because `T` is replicated), so the
103	  arrival count is uniform.
104	
105	- **Real multi-GPU (`NvshmemTransport`, the 8×H100 run):** each GPU runs its own
106	  grid over the FULL `T` (activations are replicated across TP ranks — TP shards
107	  WEIGHTS, not the batch). `n_tiles` is identical on every GPU, and within a GPU
108	  every CTA does the same `n_rounds`. The `bar.sync()` is intra-GPU (the
109	  GridBarrier); the cross-GPU join is the one-CTA `nvshmemx_barrier_block(tp_team)`
110	  inside `rendezvous` (EDIT A). So the nest is: intra-GPU `bar.sync()` →
111	  one-CTA-per-GPU `nvshmem_quiet()+nvshmemx_barrier_block` → intra-GPU
112	  `bar.sync()`, NEVER interleaved (the §1.13 / tp_nvshmem.md §1(3) deadlock rule).
113	
114	This restructure is **gated entirely behind `if constexpr (Par::kTPComm)`** so
115	the `SingleGPU` instantiation keeps the byte-identical grid-stride loop (the
116	PTX-diff gate). The detail is the reason this track is hard and is the single
117	most important thing the kernel-track implementer must get right; EDIT C.3 gives
118	the exact shape.

178	        float u_mlp[mb::kSeq][mb::kDff];       // up_proj out
179	    } act[mb::kLayers];

181	    float fn_xhat[mb::kSeq][mb::kD];
182	    float fn_r[mb::kSeq];
183	    float logits[mb::kPHead];
184	    // Backward adjoint scratch (reused across the per-block chain).

187	    float adj_a[mb::kSeq][mb::kDInner];        // d_inner-wide scratch
188	    float adj_b[mb::kSeq][mb::kDInner];        // d_inner-wide scratch
189	    float adj_c[mb::kSeq][mb::kDInner];        // d_inner-wide scratch

195	    float dCbar[mb::kSeq][mb::kStateC][2];

318	// ── Block-wide reductions (256 threads). ──────────────────────────────────────
319	__device__ __forceinline__ float mb_block_sum(float v, float* red) {
320	    const unsigned full = 0xffffffffu;
321	    #pragma unroll
322	    for (int o = 16; o > 0; o >>= 1) v += __shfl_down_sync(full, v, o);
323	    const int lane = threadIdx.x & 31, warp = threadIdx.x >> 5;
324	    if (lane == 0) red[warp] = v;
325	    __syncthreads();
326	    const int nwarp = (blockDim.x + 31) >> 5;
327	    if (warp == 0) {
328	        float p = (lane < nwarp) ? red[lane] : 0.0f;
329	        #pragma unroll
330	        for (int o = 16; o > 0; o >>= 1) p += __shfl_down_sync(full, p, o);
331	        if (lane == 0) red[0] = p;
332	    }
333	    __syncthreads();
334	    float r = red[0];
335	    __syncthreads();
336	    return r;
337	}
338	__device__ __forceinline__ float mb_block_max(float v, float* red) {
339	    const unsigned full = 0xffffffffu;
340	    #pragma unroll
341	    for (int o = 16; o > 0; o >>= 1) v = fmaxf(v, __shfl_down_sync(full, v, o));
342	    const int lane = threadIdx.x & 31, warp = threadIdx.x >> 5;
343	    if (lane == 0) red[warp] = v;
344	    __syncthreads();
345	    const int nwarp = (blockDim.x + 31) >> 5;
346	    if (warp == 0) {
347	        float p = (lane < nwarp) ? red[lane] : -CUDART_INF_F;
348	        #pragma unroll
349	        for (int o = 16; o > 0; o >>= 1) p = fmaxf(p, __shfl_down_sync(full, p, o));
350	        if (lane == 0) red[0] = p;
351	    }
352	    __syncthreads();
353	    float r = red[0];
354	    __syncthreads();
355	    return r;
356	}

358	// ── Primitive linear op (CTA-cooperative). y[s,:out] = x[s,:in] @ W[out,in]^T
359	//    (+ b). One thread per (s,o), strided. `ldX`/`ldY` are the row strides (in
360	//    elements) of x/y (so a packed view into a wider buffer works). ───────────
361	__device__ __forceinline__ void mb_linear(
362	        const float* __restrict__ x, int in_dim, int ldX,
363	        const float* __restrict__ W, const float* __restrict__ b, int out_dim,
364	        float* __restrict__ y, int ldY) {
365	    const int total = mb::kSeq * out_dim;
366	    for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < total; idx += blockDim.x) {
367	        const int s = idx / out_dim, o = idx % out_dim;
368	        const float* xr = x + (int64_t)s * ldX;
369	        const float* Wr = W + (int64_t)o * in_dim;
370	        float acc = (b != nullptr) ? b[o] : 0.0f;
371	        #pragma unroll 4
372	        for (int k = 0; k < in_dim; ++k) acc += xr[k] * Wr[k];
373	        y[(int64_t)s * ldY + o] = acc;
374	    }
375	    __syncthreads();
376	}

378	// ── RMSNorm forward over the last dim (width=D). y = x*rsqrt(mean(x^2)+eps)*w.
379	//    Caches xhat = x*r and r (per row). NO mean-subtract, NO bias (RMS, not LN).
380	//    ldX = explicit row stride of x. xhat_out/y packed D-wide. (mamba3_oracle
381	//    rmsnorm_forward.) `width` so it serves both kD (norms) and kStateC (BCNorm).
382	__device__ __forceinline__ void mb_rmsnorm_fwd(
383	        const float* __restrict__ x, const float* __restrict__ w,
384	        float* __restrict__ y, float* __restrict__ xhat_out,
385	        float* __restrict__ r_out, float* red, int width, int ldX) {
386	    for (int s = 0; s < mb::kSeq; ++s) {
387	        const float* xr = x + (int64_t)s * ldX;
388	        float ss = 0.0f;
389	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < width; j += blockDim.x) { float v = xr[j]; ss += v * v; }
390	        float ms = mb_block_sum(ss, red) / (float)width;
391	        float r = rsqrtf(ms + mb::kRmsEps);
392	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) r_out[s] = r;
393	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < width; j += blockDim.x) {
394	            float xh = xr[j] * r;
395	            xhat_out[(int64_t)s * width + j] = xh;
396	            y[(int64_t)s * width + j] = xh * w[j];
397	        }
398	        __syncthreads();
399	    }
400	}

402	// ── RMSNorm backward (mamba3_oracle rmsnorm_backward):
403	//     dw   = sum_rows (dy * xhat)
404	//     dxhat= dy * w
405	//     dx   = r * (dxhat - xhat * (sum_lastdim(dxhat*xhat) / D))
406	//    dy packed width-wide; xhat packed width-wide; dx_out packed width-wide.
407	//    gw is ACCUMULATED (+=). ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
408	__device__ inline void mb_rmsnorm_bwd(
409	        const float* __restrict__ dy, const float* __restrict__ xhat,
410	        const float* __restrict__ r, const float* __restrict__ w,
411	        float* __restrict__ dx_out, float* __restrict__ gw, float* red, int width) {
412	    for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < width; j += blockDim.x) {
413	        float dgw = 0.0f;
414	        #pragma unroll
415	        for (int s = 0; s < mb::kSeq; ++s)
416	            dgw += dy[(int64_t)s * width + j] * xhat[(int64_t)s * width + j];
417	        gw[j] += dgw;
418	    }
419	    for (int s = 0; s < mb::kSeq; ++s) {
420	        const float* dyr = dy + (int64_t)s * width;
421	        const float* xhr = xhat + (int64_t)s * width;
422	        float sdax = 0.0f;
423	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < width; j += blockDim.x) {
424	            float dxhat = dyr[j] * w[j];
425	            sdax += dxhat * xhr[j];
426	        }
427	        sdax = mb_block_sum(sdax, red);
428	        float corr = sdax / (float)width;
429	        float rs = r[s];
430	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < width; j += blockDim.x) {
431	            float dxhat = dyr[j] * w[j];
432	            dx_out[(int64_t)s * width + j] = rs * (dxhat - xhr[j] * corr);
433	        }
434	        __syncthreads();
435	    }
436	}

438	// ── dW += dY^T @ X for a linear Y = X @ W^T (+ b). dX = dY @ W (set or add).
439	//    Owner-thread per (o,i) for dW; db[o]+=Σ_s dY. ldX/ldY are x/dY row strides.─
440	__device__ inline void mb_linear_bwd(
441	        const float* __restrict__ dY, int ldY, const float* __restrict__ X, int ldX,
442	        const float* __restrict__ W, int in_dim, int out_dim,
443	        float* __restrict__ dW, float* __restrict__ db,
444	        float* __restrict__ dx_out, int ldDx, bool set_dx) {
445	    const int wtot = out_dim * in_dim;
446	    for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < wtot; idx += blockDim.x) {
447	        const int o = idx / in_dim, i = idx % in_dim;
448	        float acc = 0.0f;
449	        #pragma unroll
450	        for (int s = 0; s < mb::kSeq; ++s) acc += dY[(int64_t)s * ldY + o] * X[(int64_t)s * ldX + i];
451	        dW[(int64_t)o * in_dim + i] += acc;
452	    }
453	    if (db != nullptr) {
454	        for (int o = threadIdx.x; o < out_dim; o += blockDim.x) {
455	            float acc = 0.0f;
456	            #pragma unroll
457	            for (int s = 0; s < mb::kSeq; ++s) acc += dY[(int64_t)s * ldY + o];
458	            db[o] += acc;
459	        }
460	    }
461	    const int xtot = mb::kSeq * in_dim;
462	    for (int idx = threadIdx.x; idx < xtot; idx += blockDim.x) {
463	        const int s = idx / in_dim, i = idx % in_dim;
464	        float acc = 0.0f;
465	        for (int o = 0; o < out_dim; ++o) acc += dY[(int64_t)s * ldY + o] * W[(int64_t)o * in_dim + i];
466	        if (set_dx) dx_out[(int64_t)s * ldDx + i] = acc;
467	        else dx_out[(int64_t)s * ldDx + i] += acc;
468	    }
469	    __syncthreads();
470	}

472	// ── RMSNorm backward variant that recomputes xhat = x*r from the RAW pre-norm
473	//    input x (so callers that did NOT cache xhat — BCNorm, which caches only the
474	//    raw stream + recip — can reuse it). dx_out is written with row stride ldDx
475	//    (so it can land in a packed slice of a wider buffer). gw ACCUMULATED. ─────
476	__device__ inline void mb_rmsnorm_bwd_rawx(
477	        const float* __restrict__ dy, const float* __restrict__ x,
478	        const float* __restrict__ r, const float* __restrict__ w,
479	        float* __restrict__ dx_out, float* __restrict__ gw,
480	        float* red, int width, int ldDx) {
481	    for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < width; j += blockDim.x) {
482	        float dgw = 0.0f;
483	        #pragma unroll
484	        for (int s = 0; s < mb::kSeq; ++s)
485	            dgw += dy[(int64_t)s * width + j] * (x[(int64_t)s * width + j] * r[s]);
486	        gw[j] += dgw;
487	    }
488	    for (int s = 0; s < mb::kSeq; ++s) {
489	        const float* dyr = dy + (int64_t)s * width;
490	        const float* xr  = x  + (int64_t)s * width;
491	        float rs = r[s];
492	        float sdax = 0.0f;
493	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < width; j += blockDim.x) {
494	            float xhat = xr[j] * rs;
495	            float dxhat = dyr[j] * w[j];
496	            sdax += dxhat * xhat;
497	        }
498	        sdax = mb_block_sum(sdax, red);
499	        float corr = sdax / (float)width;
500	        for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < width; j += blockDim.x) {
501	            float xhat = xr[j] * rs;
502	            float dxhat = dyr[j] * w[j];
503	            dx_out[(int64_t)s * ldDx + j] = rs * (dxhat - xhat * corr);
504	        }
505	        __syncthreads();
506	    }
507	}

510	//  COMPLEX EXPONENTIAL-TRAPEZOIDAL SELECTIVE SCAN — forward (Eq 25). One thread
511	//  owns SSM channel j in [0,d_inner). Its head is h = j/head_dim. Within the
